scope: Proposition 6.4 (Causal exposure for mixed prescriptions) of the manuscript “The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals” (preprints/The-Boltzmann-Grad-limit-for-stable-radial-potentials-on-regular-kinetic-intervals-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce9fe5976f17b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an admissible mixed whole-cell prescription with p ≤ Pa labels and a total energy budget K ≤ Rp. Fix a collection of k disjoint regular terminal trees as in Lemma 6.2. Sum the absolute activity-normalized chart integrals over the event that every selected tree has a first defect. The result is bounded by Ap (pJ)Cp(︁ pC εc)︁k/2 , (6.10) The factor (pJ)Cp includes cell-segment choices. Constants may depend on the fixed layer count, compact cutoffs, M, and R.
